correctness.rationale: For each n>=3 polygon, its boundary radius in a direction δ from nearest vertex is r/cos(α−δ), α=π/n,r=Rcosα. A circle t∈(r,R) is covered by vertex-angle arcs of half-width η=α−arccos(r/t). With m cyclic phase gaps g_j summing 2α, angular measure exactly nΣ min(g_j,2η), valid also for zero gaps. The sharp sum inequality Σmin(g,c)≤min(2α,mc) has all-level equality for equal gaps; unequal gaps are strictly inferior on an open interval near c=2α/m, so positive-a.e. radial weights strictly prefer equal gaps. The polar angular integration per gap equals r²[tanα−tan(α−g/2)], giving area/inradius and the stated 1/m disk deficit. Independent Shapely computations for (n,m)=(3,3),(4,3) with coincident phases,(5,5),(7,2) agree with the exact formula <1e−10. These finite cases are diagnostics, not the all-n,m proof.
